deviations.what: The wooden pipe renders as a cube instead of a centre with arms.
deviations.why: The block-entity rendering hook (set_custom_render) draws a block's own geometry on all five loaders, but the pipe does not use it yet, so it still draws as its cube.

deviations.what: The wooden pipe moves items one slot at a time instead of via travelling item entities.
deviations.why: The port starts with the observable chest-to-chest behaviour; the reference routes through a connection matrix.

deviations.what: The wooden pipe chooses its extraction side automatically instead of storing it in the block's metadata.
deviations.why: The port has no block metadata access or wrench yet; the reference stores the side in the pipe's metadata and cycles it with a wrench (PipeLogicWood.switchSource).

deviations.what: Which slots of an inventory another block may use is a slot range the block entity declares, rather than the reference's side-aware ISpecialInventory.
deviations.why: The reference asks the neighbour inventory itself, per side and per item (ISpecialInventory.addItem and extractItem). grug exports can only be called by the host and cannot return a value, so the rule is declared to the host instead and read back with is_slot_extractable.

deviations.what: The redstone engine draws its piston plate at rest instead of moving it, and the chamber under it, at its stage's piston speed.
deviations.why: The engine draws through render(), which builds chunk geometry once per redraw, and a stroke that moves every tick needs a redraw per tick or a per-frame rendering hook grug does not have. The stage still shows as the trunk's colour.

deviations.what: The redstone engine gives no energy to the pipe it powers and takes none from another engine, so its energy is never capped at 1000 and it never explodes.
deviations.why: The port has no model of BuildCraft's pneumatic power: the wooden pipe runs from the engine's redstone signal instead of from extracted energy. A wood engine on redstone alone never caps or explodes in the reference either, since EngineWood.update adds to its energy directly rather than through addEnergy.

deviations.what: The redstone engine always faces up, instead of turning to face a power receptor when placed and rotating with a wrench.
deviations.why: TileEngine saves its orientation in its NBT and RenderEngine draws the engine along it, but the port has no receptor to face and no wrench yet, and its model is drawn upright only.

deviations.what: The redstone engine's faces are lit from the block each face looks towards, with the game's per-side shade, instead of drawn with GL lighting off.
deviations.why: RenderEngine disables GL lighting while it draws the engine, and the engine's block is not opaque, but a grug block is opaque, so its own position is dark and its faces borrow the neighbour's light. The exact brightness 2.2.14 draws with has not been worked out yet.

deviations.what: The redstone engine's item is drawn with the piston plate at rest, and its drawing was never measured against 2.2.14's inventory render.
deviations.why: RenderEngine.inventoryRender draws the blue trunk with the plate at progress 0.25, and Alpha's GUI needed the model mirrored to show the faces the other block items show. Neither has been compared with a reference run.
